en: 6. Saṅkhāra Yamaka 6.2 Pavattivāra 6.2.2.
Nirodhavāra (The Chapter on Cessation)
6.2.2.1. Chapter on the Present (Paccuppannavāra) 6.2.2.1.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation ceases, for that person does verbal formation cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation in those who are without applied thought and sustained thought, their bodily formation ceases,
but their verbal formation does not cease. At the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation in those who have attained the first jhāna and in those of the sense-sphere,
both their bodily formation and their verbal formation cease.
Or again, for whom verbal formation ceases, does bodily formation cease for them?
For those at the moment of the dissolution of applied thought and sustained thought without inhalation and exhalation, verbal formation ceases, but bodily formation does not cease for them.
For those who have attained the first jhāna and for sense-sphere beings [at the moment of the dissolution of] inhalation and exhalation...
At the moment of dissolution, both verbal formation and bodily formation cease for them.
For whom bodily formation ceases, does mental formation also cease for that person? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom mental formation ceases, does bodily formation also cease for that person?
At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness in one who is without inhalation and exhalation, their mental formation ceases,
but their bodily formation does not cease. At the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation,
both their mental formation and their bodily formation cease.
Does the verbal formation cease for that person for whom the mental formation ceases? Yes.
Or rather, does the verbal formation cease for that person for whom the mental formation ceases?
At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness when it is devoid of applied thought and sustained thought, the mental formation ceases for them, but the verbal formation does not.
For them, verbal formation ceases. At the moment of the dissolution of applied thought and sustained thought, for them both mental formation and verbal formation cease.
6.2.2.1.2. Positive Order: Scope (Anuloma-okāsa)
Where bodily formation ceases, does verbal formation cease there?
…pe…. 6.2.2.1.3. Positive Person-Space:
For whom, where bodily formation ceases, for that person does verbal formation cease there? …pe…. (The "for whom" [yassaka] and "for whom, where" [yassay-attha] sections are identical.)
6.2.2.1.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala) Does bodily formation not cease for one in whom verbal formation does not cease?
For those who are without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the dissolution of applied thought and sustained thought, bodily formation does not cease.
Yet, for them, verbal formation does not cease. For all those at the moment of the arising of consciousness, excluding those without breath-in and breath-out;

for those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness without initial application and sustained application; and for those who have attained cessation and non-percipient beings—for them, neither bodily formation nor verbal formation ceases.
Or again, for whom verbal formation does not cease, for that person does bodily formation not cease?

At the moment of dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, excluding those [states] accompanied by initial application and sustained application (*vitakka-vicāra*), verbal formation does not cease for them, but bodily formation does not fail to cease for them.
For all [beings], at the moment of arising of consciousness, excluding inhalation and exhalation...

At the moment of the cessation of a mind without applied thought or sustained thought, and for those who have attained the attainment of cessation or are non-percipient beings, neither verbal formation nor bodily formation ceases.
For whom bodily formation does not cease, does mental formation not cease for them?
In those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the mind’s dissolution, the bodily formation does not cease,
yet the mental formation does not fail to cease. In all those at the moment of the mind’s arising,
in those who have attained cessation, and in non-percipient beings, neither the bodily formation nor the mental formation ceases.
Or for whomsoever... [as before] ...? Yes.
For whom verbal formation does not cease, does mental formation not cease for him?

At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness (cittassa bhaṅgakkhaṇe) without initial application and sustained application (vitakka-vicāra), for those persons verbal formation does not cease, but [mental formation does not necessarily cease].

For them, the mental formation does not cease. For all those at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those who have attained cessation, and for non-percipient beings, neither the verbal formation nor the mental formation ceases.
Or, for whom...? Yes, it is so.
6.2.2.1.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where bodily formation does not cease … [as above] … 6.2.2.1.6.
Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom and where the bodily formation does not cease, for them and there the verbal formation does not cease?

Excluding inhalation and exhalation, at the moment of the dissolution of applied and sustained thought, for them and there the bodily formation does not cease, but it is not the case that the verbal formation does not cease for them and there.
[This is so] for all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, excluding...
In the moment of dissolution of a mind without initial application and sustained application due to in-breaths and out-breaths, and in the case of non-percipient beings,
neither the bodily formation nor the verbal formation ceases there. Or, conversely,
for whomsoever and wherever the verbal formation does not cease … [and so on] … [as before].

(The sections for "whichever" and "whichever person" should be expanded in the same manner; however, in the section for "whichever person," the phrase "those who have attained cessation" [nirodhasamāpannānaṃ] should not be used.
6.2.2.2. Past Section (Atītavāra) 6.2.2.2.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala)
For whom bodily formation had ceased, for that person had verbal formation ceased? Yes.

Or conversely...? Yes. (Just as in the section on arising, the past questions—those concerning "for whom," those concerning "for whom and for what," the positive, and the negative—were analyzed, so too should they be analyzed here in the section on cessation; there is no difference.)
6.2.2.3. Chapter on the Future (Anāgatavāra) 6.2.2.3.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) will cease, for that person will verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) cease? Yes.
Or conversely, for whom verbal formation will cease, will bodily formation also cease for that person?

For those in the sense-sphere at the moment of the arising of their final consciousness; for those whose consciousness immediately following it will give rise to the final consciousness of the sense-sphere;
for those final-existence beings in the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere; and for those [in the fine-material sphere] who...
For those who, having been reborn in the formless realm, will attain final nibbāna there, at the moment of their death, verbal formation will cease,
but bodily formation will not cease for them. For others, both verbal formation and bodily formation will cease.
For whom bodily formation will cease, for that person will mental formation cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom mental formation will cease, for that person will bodily formation cease?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm, and for that consciousness immediately after which [there arises] [another] consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm...
For those whose final consciousness will arise in the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere— namely,
those in their last existence in the fine-material or immaterial spheres who will attain final Nibbāna upon rebirth— and for those passing away [from there], mental formation will cease,
but bodily formation will not cease for them. For others, both mental formation and bodily formation will cease.
The bodily formation will cease.
For whom the verbal formation will cease, will the mental formation cease for that person? Yes.
Or rather, for whom the mental formation will cease, will the verbal formation cease for that person?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness which is without applied thought and sustained thought, and for those whose consciousness immediately following it will arise as the final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought,
mental formation will cease, but vocal formation will not cease for them. For others, both mental formation and vocal formation will cease.
6.2.2.3.2. Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa): Where bodily formation will cease … [etc.
… 6.2.2.3.3. Positive Person-Plane (Anuloma-puggalokāsa)
For whom and where will bodily formation cease, will vocal formation also cease for them there?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna, bodily formation will cease there, but vocal formation will not cease for them there.
For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those of the sense-sphere realm...
In those [beings], both the bodily formation and the verbal formation will cease there.
Or rather, for whomsoever the verbal formation will cease at a certain place, will the bodily formation also cease for that person at that same place?
[It will] for those of the sense-sphere at the moment of the arising of their final consciousness, and for those of the sense-sphere immediately after whichever consciousness [has arisen].
For those of the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere whose final consciousness is about to arise,

verbal formation will cease there, but bodily formation will not cease for them there. For those who have attained the first jhāna and for others belonging to the sense-sphere, both verbal formation and bodily formation will cease there.
For whom and where the bodily formation will cease, for that person and in that place will the mental formation cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom and where the mental formation will cease, for that person and in that place will the bodily formation cease?

[It will not] in the case of the arising moment of the final consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm, nor for that consciousness immediately after which [a consciousness of] those in the sense-sphere realm [arises].

For those who have attained the fourth jhāna—whether belonging to the fine-material sphere (rūpāvacara) or the immaterial sphere (arūpāvacara)—their mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) will cease there at the final consciousness;
yet their bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) will not cease there.
For those who have attained the first, second, or third jhānas, and for others belonging to the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara), [the same applies].
In that case, both the mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) will cease and the bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) will cease.
For whomsoever, wherever vocal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) will cease, for that person there, will mental formation also cease? Yes.
Or conversely, for whomsoever, wherever mental formation will cease, for that person there, will vocal formation also cease?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness that is without applied thought and sustained thought, and for those who have attained the second jhāna, the third jhāna, or the fourth jhāna— such that immediately after this consciousness the final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought will arise—
the mental formation (cittasaṅkhāra) will cease therein, but the verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) will not cease therein for them.

For those who have attained the first jhāna, for those of the sense-sphere realm, and for others of the fine-material and immaterial realms—therein, both the mental formation and the verbal formation will cease.
6.2.2.3.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala).
For whom bodily formation will not cease, for that person will verbal formation not cease?
At the moment of arising of the final consciousness of those in the sense-sphere; for those whose consciousness immediately following it the final consciousness of the sense-sphere will arise;
for those final-existence beings in the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere; and for those [who will be reborn] in the fine-material sphere...
For those who will attain final Nibbāna after being reborn in the formless realm, at the moment of their death, bodily formation will not cease, but verbal formation will not fail to cease.

At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought; for those possessing the final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought; and for one whose consciousness immediately following [this] is without applied thought and sustained thought...
For those in whom the final consciousness will arise, both bodily formation and verbal formation will not cease.
Or for whomsoever … [as before] … Yes.
For whom bodily formation will not cease, will mental formation not cease for him?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness of those in the sense-sphere realm; for those whose consciousness immediately following it will give rise to the final consciousness of the sense-sphere realm;

for those in the fine-material or immaterial realms who are in their final existence; and for those who, having been reborn in the fine-material or immaterial realms, will attain final Nibbāna while passing away—for all these, bodily formation does not [arise].
It will cease, but for them mental formation will not cease. At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for those persons both bodily formation and mental formation will not cease.
Or, for whom...? Yes, they will.
For whom verbal formation will not cease, for that person will mental formation not cease?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness which is without initial application and sustained application, and for those whose final consciousness without initial application and sustained application will arise immediately after that consciousness—
verbal formation will not cease for them, but mental formation will not [necessarily] not cease for them.
It will not cease. At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for those persons, both verbal formation and mental formation will not cease.
Or, for whom...? Yes, it is so.
6.2.2.3.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where bodily formation will not cease …pe… 6.2.2.3.6.
Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom, where bodily formation will not cease, for that person there verbal formation will not cease?
For those of the sense-sphere at the moment of the arising of the final consciousness; for those whose consciousness immediately following it the final consciousness of the sense-sphere will arise;
and for those of the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—therein, for them, bodily formation [will not cease].
It will not cease, yet for them there verbal formation will not fail to cease there.

At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought; for those possessing the final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought; for those whose consciousness immediately following it will give rise to the final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought;
for those who have attained the fourth jhāna; and for non-percipient beings—for these, there [verbal formation] will not cease there.
Will bodily formation not cease and verbal formation also not cease?
Or conversely, for whomsoever and wherever verbal formation will not cease, for that person there bodily formation will not cease?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna, verbal formation will not cease therein.
And yet, for them, the bodily formation will not cease there. [This is the case] at the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by applied and sustained thought;

for those possessing the final consciousness without applied or sustained thought; for those whose final consciousness without applied or sustained thought will arise immediately after this consciousness;
for those who have attained the fourth jhāna; and for non-percipient beings—for these, the bodily formation does not cease there.
The verbal formation will not cease and the bodily formation will not cease.
For whom and where the bodily formation will not cease, for that person and in that place, will the mental formation not cease?
At the moment of the arising of the final consciousness of those in the sense sphere (kāmāvacara), and for that consciousness immediately preceding [the death-moment] of those in the sense sphere...
For those who have attained the fourth jhāna— whether belonging to the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere—
and for whom the final consciousness is about to arise, there the bodily formation will not cease, yet it is not the case that the mental formation will not cease for them there.
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, and for non-percipient beings, both the bodily formation and the mental formation will not cease there.
And will the mental formation not cease?
Or, for whomsoever and wherever the mental formation will not cease, will the bodily formation not cease for that person there? Yes.
For whomsoever and wherever the verbal formation will not cease, will the mental formation not cease for that person there?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness that is without applied thought and sustained thought, and for those who have attained the second jhāna, the third jhāna, or the fourth jhāna— the consciousness immediately after which the final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought will arise—
therein vocal formation will not cease, but mental formation will not fail to cease for them there.
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, and for non-percipient beings, neither verbal formation nor mental formation will cease there. Or rather:
for whomsoever mental formation will not cease in a certain place, will verbal formation also not cease for that person in that same place? Yes.
6.2.2.4. Chapter on the Present and the Past (Paccuppannātītavāra) 6.2.2.4.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) ceases, for that person did verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom verbal formation has ceased, does bodily formation cease for them?
For all those at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness when breath-in and breath-out are absent,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings— verbal formation has ceased for them, but bodily formation does not cease for them.

At the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, verbal formation has ceased and bodily formation ceases. In all [beings] at the moment of arising of consciousness, and in those at the moment of dissolution of consciousness when there is no inhalation or exhalation,
and in those who have attained cessation and non-percipient beings, mental formation has ceased, but bodily formation does not cease for them.
At the moment of dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, for them both mental formation and bodily formation have ceased.
For whom verbal formation ceases, for that person has mental formation ceased? Yes.
Or rather, for whom mental formation has ceased, for that person does verbal formation cease?

[It does not] for all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those without initial application and sustained application, for those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those who have attained cessation.
For those non-percipient beings, the mental formation had ceased, but the verbal formation does not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of applied and sustained thought, for those [beings], both the mental formation and the verbal formation have ceased.
6.2.2.4.2. Positive Spatial Analysis (Anuloma-okāsa)
Where bodily formation ceases … [etc.
… 6.2.2.4.3. Positive Person-Space Correlation:
For whom and where bodily formation ceases, for that person and in that place, had verbal formation ceased?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation,
the bodily formation ceases therein, but the verbal formation has not yet ceased for them there. For those who have attained the first jhāna,
or for sense-sphere beings at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, the bodily formation [ceases therein].
And does verbal formation cease? Or, conversely, where verbal formation has ceased, does bodily formation cease there for that person?
For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those in the sense-sphere at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation—for these very persons...
In the absence of inhalation and exhalation, at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those belonging to the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere,
verbal formation has ceased there, but bodily formation does not cease there for them.
For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those of the sense-sphere at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, verbal formation [has ceased] there for them.
And [it is such that] the bodily formation has ceased and the bodily formation is ceasing.
For whomsoever, wherever the bodily formation ceases, for that person there, has the mental formation ceased? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever, wherever the mental formation has ceased, for that person there, does the bodily formation cease?
In all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and in those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the cessation of consciousness:
for them, there the mental formation has ceased, but the bodily formation does not cease. At the moment of the cessation of inhalation and exhalation:
for them, there both the mental formation has ceased and the bodily formation ceases.
For whom and where verbal formation ceases, for that person does mental formation cease there? Yes.
Or rather, for whom and where mental formation has ceased, for that person does verbal formation cease there?

For all [beings] at the moment of arising of consciousness, and for those without initial application and sustained application at the moment of dissolution of consciousness—for them, there [verbal formation does not cease].

The mental formation had ceased for them, but the verbal formation does not cease for them there. At the moment of the dissolution of applied thought and sustained thought, both the mental formation and the verbal formation have ceased for them there.
6.2.2.4.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala)
For whom bodily formation does not cease, for that person did verbal formation not cease? It did cease.
Or rather, for whom verbal formation did not cease, for that person does bodily formation not cease? There is no such case.
For whom bodily formation does not cease, for that person did mental formation not cease? It did cease.
Or, for whom mental formation had not ceased, does bodily formation not cease for him? None.
For whom verbal formation does not cease, had mental formation not ceased for him? It had ceased.
Or, for whom mental formation had not ceased, does verbal formation not cease for him? None.
6.2.2.4.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa):
Where bodily formation does not cease … [etc. … 6.2.2.4.6.
Negative Person and Plane (Paccanīka-puggalokāsa)
For whom, where bodily formation does not cease, for that person there verbal formation has not ceased?
For those who have attained the first jhāna; for those in the sense-sphere at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation;

for those same persons at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation; and for those in the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—for these, there [verbal formation] has not ceased.
The bodily formation does not cease, yet for them the verbal formation has not ceased there.

This is the case for those who have attained the second or third jhāna at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation; for those same persons at the moment of the cessation of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation;
for those who have attained the fourth jhāna; and for the inhabitants of the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa) while their second moment of consciousness is occurring.
For non-percipient beings, neither the bodily formation nor the verbal formation has ceased there.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever the verbal formation has not ceased at a certain place, does the bodily formation not cease for them there?
For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna, and at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, [neither has ceased] there.
Verbal formation has not ceased, yet bodily formation does not fail to cease for them there.

This is the case for those who have attained the second or third jhāna at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation; for those very persons, at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation;
and for those who have attained the fourth jhāna, or for the inhabitants of the Pure Abodes (suddhāvāsa) while their second moment of consciousness is occurring.
For non-percipient beings, neither verbal formation nor bodily formation has ceased there.
For whomsoever bodily formation does not cease in a certain place, has mental formation not ceased for them there? [Answer:

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, [mental formation has not ceased] there.

Body formation does not cease, yet mental formation has not ceased for them there. For those beings reborn in the Pure Abodes and for non-percipient beings, neither body formation nor mental formation has ceased there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever mental formation has not ceased there, does body formation not cease for them there? Yes.
For whom and where verbal formation does not cease, for that person and in that place, had mental formation not ceased?

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the cessation of consciousness when it is devoid of applied thought and sustained thought, verbal formation does not cease there;
yet, for them, mental formation had not ceased there. [This applies to those born in] the Pure Abodes...
For those beings who are being reborn among the non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), neither verbal formation (*vacī-saṅkhāra*) nor mental formation (*citta-saṅkhāra*) ceases there. Or, conversely:
for whomsoever mental formation has not ceased at a certain place, does verbal formation not cease for them there? Yes, it does.
6.2.2.5. Chapter on the Present and Future (Paccuppannānāgatavāra)
6.2.2.5.1. Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation ceases, for that person will verbal formation cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom verbal formation will cease, for that person does bodily formation cease?
In all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness when there is no in-breathing or out-breathing,
and in those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, verbal formation will cease, but bodily formation does not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of in-breathing and out-breathing, both verbal formation and bodily formation cease for them.
Is it the case that for whom bodily formation ceases, for him mental formation will cease? Yes.
Or rather, is it the case that for whom mental formation will cease, for him bodily formation ceases?

[It is not so] for all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those without inhalation and exhalation, for those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, and for those who have entered the attainment of cessation.
For non-percipient beings, mental formation will cease, but bodily formation does not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, both mental formation and bodily formation cease for them.
For one whose verbal formation ceases, will mental formation cease for that person?

At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, verbal formation ceases for them, but mental formation will not cease for them. At the moment of the cessation of other applied thought and sustained thought,
both verbal formation and mental formation cease for them.
Or, for whomsoever mental formation will cease, does verbal formation cease for that person?
For all those at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those at the moment of the cessation of consciousness (excluding initial application and sustained application),
and for those who have attained the attainment of cessation or are non-percipient beings— mental formation will cease for them, but verbal formation does not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of applied thought (*vitakka*) and sustained thought (*vicāra*), both the mental formation (*cittasaṅkhāra*) and the verbal formation (*vacīsaṅkhāra*) cease for them.
6.2.2.5.2. Positive Plane Analysis:
Wherever the bodily formation (*kāyasaṅkhāra*) ceases … [and so forth] … pe … [as above].
6.2.2.5.3. Positive Person-Space (Anuloma-puggalokāsa) In whom, and where, bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) ceases, will verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) cease for them there?
For those who have attained the second jhāna and the third jhāna, at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, for them there—
The bodily formation ceases, but the verbal formation will not cease for them there.
For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those in the sense-sphere at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation,
both the bodily formation and the verbal formation cease there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever and wherever verbal formation will cease, does bodily formation cease for them there?

[It does not. For those who have attained the first jhāna, for those in the sense-sphere at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation, for those same persons at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness without inhalation and exhalation, and for those in the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—for these, bodily formation ceases there, but verbal formation will not cease.
Verbal formation will cease, but bodily formation does not cease for them there.
For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those in the sense-sphere at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation,
both verbal formation and bodily formation cease there.
For whom and wherein the bodily formation ceases, for that person and therein will the mental formation cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom and wherein the mental formation will cease, for that person and therein does the bodily formation cease?

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness—at these, for them and therein [the bodily formation does not cease].

The mental formation will cease, but the bodily formation does not cease for them there. At the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, both the mental formation and the bodily formation cease for them there.
For whomsoever the verbal formation ceases there, will the mental formation also cease for that person there?
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, verbal formation ceases for them there,
but mental formation will not cease for them there. At the moment of the cessation of other applied thought and sustained thought,
both verbal formation and mental formation cease for them there.
Or conversely: for whomsoever and wherever the mental formation (*cittasaṅkhāra*) will cease, does the verbal formation (*vacīsaṅkhāra*) cease for them there?

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness when it is devoid of initial application (*vitakka*) and sustained application (*vicāra*), the mental formation will cease there, but the verbal formation does not cease for them there. [This is so] for initial application and sustained application...
At the moment of dissolution, for those [beings], there the mental formation will cease and the verbal formation ceases.
6.2.2.5.4. Negative Person (Paccanīka-puggala):
For whom bodily formation does not cease, for that person will verbal formation not cease?

In all beings at the moment of the arising of consciousness, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness when there is no breathing in or out, and in those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings, bodily formation does not cease; yet verbal formation will not fail to cease in them.

[This is also the case] at the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness accompanied by initial and sustained application, and in those possessing the final consciousness without initial or sustained application.
For those whose final consciousness will arise immediately after a state of consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought, neither the bodily formation nor the verbal formation ceases.
Or rather, for whomsoever the verbal formation will not cease, does the bodily formation not cease for them? Yes, it does.
For whom bodily formation does not cease, for that person will mental formation not cease?
For all those at the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those without inhalation and exhalation at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness,
and for those who have attained cessation or are non-percipient beings— bodily formation does not cease for them, yet it is not the case that mental formation will not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for those persons, the bodily formation does not cease and the mental formation will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever... [as before]... Yes.
For whomsoever the verbal formation does not cease, for him the mental formation will not cease? Yes.

In all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness when it is devoid of initial application and sustained application, in those who have attained the attainment of cessation, and in non-percipient beings, verbal formation does not cease; yet mental formation will not fail to cease in them.
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness that is without initial application and sustained application, in those [beings], verbal formation does not cease.
And the mental formation will not cease.
Or, for whom the mental formation will not cease, does the verbal formation not cease for that person?
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, for those [beings], the mental formation will not cease.

And yet, their verbal formation does not cease. At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness, which is without applied thought and sustained thought, both their mental formation will not cease and their verbal formation does not cease.
6.2.2.5.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-okāsa)
Where bodily formation does not cease ... [as before] ... 6.2.2.5.6.
Negative Person-Space:
For whom, where bodily formation does not cease, will verbal formation not cease for that person there?
For those who have attained the first jhāna, at the moment of the arising of in-breaths and out-breaths belonging to the sense sphere;
for those same persons, at the moment of the cessation of consciousness occurring without in-breaths and out-breaths;

and for those belonging to the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere—at these times, bodily formation does not cease therein, yet verbal formation will not fail to cease therein. [This applies] to the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought.

At the moment of dissolution of consciousness for those possessing the final consciousness that is without initial application and sustained application; for those whose final consciousness, immediately following this consciousness, will arise as one without initial application and sustained application;
for those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of arising of inhalation and exhalation;
and for those same persons at the moment of dissolution of consciousness when there is no inhalation or exhalation—[these are the conditions] for the fourth jhāna.
For those who have attained the attainment of non-percipient beings, there the bodily formation does not cease and the verbal formation will not cease. Or, conversely,
for whomsoever the verbal formation will not cease at a certain place, does the bodily formation not cease for that person at that place?

For those who have attained the second jhāna or the third jhāna at the moment of the dissolution of inhalation and exhalation, verbal formation will not cease there, but bodily formation does not fail to cease for them there.

At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by applied and sustained thought; for those possessing the final consciousness without applied or sustained thought; and for one whose consciousness immediately following [the present] is without applied or sustained thought—
For those who have attained the second or third jhāna and whose final consciousness is about to arise; for those at the moment of the arising of inhalation and exhalation;
for those at the moment of the cessation of that very same consciousness when it is devoid of inhalation and exhalation;
for those who have attained the fourth jhāna; and for non-percipient beings—in these cases, neither verbal formation nor bodily formation ceases there.
For whom and where the bodily formation does not cease, for that person and there will the mental formation not cease?

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness when breath-in and breath-out are absent, the bodily formation does not cease there;
yet it is not the case that for them the mental formation will not cease there. [This applies to] the final consciousness...
At the moment of dissolution, for non-percipient beings, neither the bodily formation nor the mental formation ceases there.
Or, for whom...? Yes, [for all].
For whom and where verbal formation does not cease, for that person and there will mental formation not cease?

For all [beings] at the moment of the arising of consciousness, and for those at the moment of the dissolution of consciousness when it is devoid of applied thought and sustained thought—verbal formation does not cease for them there, yet mental formation will not fail to cease for them there. [This is so] for the final consciousness that is without applied thought and sustained thought.
At the moment of dissolution, for non-percipient beings, neither verbal formation nor mental formation ceases there. Or conversely:
for whomsoever mental formation will not cease at a certain place, does verbal formation not cease for them there?
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness accompanied by initial application and sustained application, mental formation will not cease for them there,
yet verbal formation does not fail to cease for them there. At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness unaccompanied by initial application and sustained application,
and for non-percipient beings, neither mental formation nor verbal formation ceases there.
6.2.2.6. Section on the Past and Future (Atītānāgatavāra) 6.2.2.6.1.
Positive Person (Anulomapuggala) For whom bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) has ceased, will verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) cease for that person?
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought;

for those possessing the final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought; and for those whose final consciousness without applied thought and sustained thought will arise immediately after the present consciousness—in these cases, bodily formation has ceased, but vocal formation will not cease. For others, bodily formation...
And verbal formation has ceased and will also cease.
Or, for whomsoever... [as before] ...? Yes.
For whomsoever bodily formation has ceased, will mental formation cease for him?

At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, bodily formation has ceased for them, but mental formation will not cease for them. For others, however, both bodily formation has ceased and mental formation will cease.
Or, for whomsoever... [as before] ...Yes.
For whomsoever verbal formation has ceased, will mental formation cease for him?

At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, verbal formation has ceased for them, but mental formation will not cease for them. For others, both verbal formation has ceased and mental formation will cease.
Or, for whom...? Yes. 6.2.2.6.2.
Positive Plane (Anuloma-okāsa)
Wherein the bodily formation has ceased … [as above] … 6.2.2.6.3. Positive Person-Space:
For whom, wherein the bodily formation has ceased, will the verbal formation cease therein?
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness in the sense sphere, and for those who have attained the second or third jhāna,
bodily formation has ceased there, but vocal formation will not cease there for them.
For those who have attained the first jhāna and for others in the sense sphere, bodily formation has not ceased there.
And the verbal formation will cease.
Or, for whomsoever and wherever the verbal formation will cease, has the bodily formation ceased for them there?
For those of the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, the verbal formation will cease there, but the bodily formation has not ceased for them.

In that case, the bodily formation had ceased. For those who have attained the first jhāna and for those belonging to the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara), both the verbal formation will cease and the bodily formation has ceased there.
If the bodily formation has ceased for someone in a certain place, will the mental formation cease for that person in that same place?
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness in the sense sphere, for those [beings], the bodily formation has ceased there,

but the mental formation will not cease there. For those who have attained the first jhāna, the second jhāna, or the third jhāna, and for others in the sense sphere, both the bodily formation and the mental formation have ceased there and will also cease there.
Or conversely: for whomsoever mental formation will cease at a certain place, has bodily formation ceased for them there?

For those who have attained the fourth jhāna, for those of the fine-material sphere, and for those of the immaterial sphere—mental formation will cease for them there, but bodily formation has not ceased for them there. [This is so] for those who have attained the first jhāna or the second jhāna.
For those of the sense-sphere realm who have attained the third jhāna, there both the mental formation and the bodily formation will cease therein.
For whomsoever the verbal formation has ceased therein, will the mental formation also cease for them therein?
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness in the plane of initial application and sustained application, verbal formation has ceased for them there,
but mental formation will not cease for them there. For others in the plane of initial application and sustained application,
both verbal formation and mental formation have ceased and will also cease there.
Or conversely, for whomsoever mental formation will cease at a certain plane, has verbal formation ceased for them at that plane?
In the plane without initial application and sustained application (*avitakka-avicāra-bhūmi*), mental formation will cease for them there, but verbal formation has not ceased for them there.
In the plane with initial application and sustained application (*savitakka-savicāra-bhūmi*), mental formation [will cease] for them there...
The verbal formation will cease and the bodily formation has ceased.
6.2.2.6.4. Negative Person:
For whom the bodily formation has not ceased, will the verbal formation not cease for them? None.
Or, for whom verbal formation will not cease, had bodily formation not ceased for him? It had ceased.
For whom bodily formation had not ceased, will mental formation not cease for him? There is none.
Or, for whom mental formation will not cease, had bodily formation not ceased for him? It had ceased.
For whom verbal formation had not ceased, will mental formation not cease for that person? There is none.
Or rather, for whom mental formation will not cease, had verbal formation not ceased for that person? It had ceased.
6.2.2.6.5. Negative Plane (Paccanīka-Okāsa)
Where bodily formation has not ceased... 6.2.2.6.6.
Negative Person-Space: For whom, where bodily formation has not ceased, will verbal formation not cease there?
For those belonging to the fine-material sphere and the immaterial sphere, bodily formation has not ceased there, but verbal formation will not fail to cease for them there.
[This is the case] at the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness accompanied by initial application and sustained application in the fine-material and immaterial spheres;

for those possessing the final consciousness without initial application and sustained application; and for one whose consciousness immediately following [the present one] is without initial application and sustained application.
For those who have attained the fourth jhāna and for non-percipient beings, the final consciousness will arise;
for them, there at that time, the bodily formation had not ceased and the verbal formation will not cease.
Or, conversely, for whomsoever the verbal formation will not cease at a certain place, for him has the bodily formation not ceased there?
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness in the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara), for those who have attained the second or third jhāna,
verbal formation (vacīsaṅkhāra) will not cease there, but bodily formation (kāyasaṅkhāra) has not failed to cease there for them.

[This is also the case] in the fine-material sphere (rūpāvacara) and the immaterial sphere (arūpāvacara) at the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness accompanied by initial and sustained application (savitakkasavicāra), and for those possessing the final consciousness without initial or sustained application (avitakka-avicāra).
In the case of one whose final consciousness, which is without initial application and sustained application, will arise immediately after that consciousness— namely,
for those who have attained the fourth jhāna or for non-percipient beings— there, neither verbal formation nor bodily formation has ceased.
For whomsoever bodily formation has not ceased in a certain place, will mental formation not cease for them in that same place?
For those who have attained the fourth jhāna, whether belonging to the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere, bodily formation has not ceased there;

yet mental formation will not fail to cease for them there. For those in the fine-material sphere or the immaterial sphere at the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, and for non-percipient beings, bodily formation has not ceased there, and...
And the mental formation will not cease.
Or, for whomsoever and wherever the mental formation will not cease, for that person there, had the bodily formation not already ceased?
At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness in the sense-sphere realm, for those persons, the mental formation will not cease there.

And yet, for them, bodily formation had not ceased there. For those in the fine-material sphere, the immaterial sphere, at the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, and for non-percipient beings, mental formation will not cease there and bodily formation had not ceased there.
For whomsoever verbal formation had not ceased in a certain place, for that person will mental formation not cease there?
In the plane without applied thought and sustained thought, for those [beings], verbal formation has not ceased there,
but mental formation will not fail to cease there. At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness in the plane without applied thought and sustained thought,
and for non-percipient beings, both verbal formation and mental formation have not ceased there, nor will mental formation cease there.
Or rather: For whomsoever mental formation will not cease at a certain place, for that person has verbal formation not ceased at that place?

At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness on the plane with applied thought and sustained thought, for those persons mental formation will not cease there, but it is not the case that verbal formation has not ceased there for them. On the plane without applied thought and sustained thought...

At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, and for those non-percipient beings, there neither will cease nor has ceased the mental formation (*cittasaṅkhāra*) and the verbal formation (*vacīsaṅkhāra*) therein.
This concludes the section on cessation.
